title: The COVID-19 social media infodemic
screen_reason: Comparative analysis of 1,342,103 posts and 7,465,721 comments about COVID-19 collected by keyword from Twitter, Instagram, YouTube, Reddit and Gab (1 January - 14 February 2020). Posts containing an external URL were matched to the Media Bias/Fact Check outlet list and labelled Questionable or Reliable; Table 4 reports, per platform, the fraction of matched link-posts that point to questionable sources (Gab 0.38, Twitter 0.10, YouTube 0.064, Instagram 0.05, Reddit 0.045). These are shares of user-posted links classified unreliable via a source-reliability list, with a stated denominator, so they are extractable. Per the denominator rule, '% of shared links unreliable' is SHARING (content_share), not CONTENT.

estimates.country: Global (no country restriction; keyword-based collection of worldwide COVID-19 content)
estimates.measure_type: % of COVID-19 posts containing an external URL matched to the MBFC outlet list that point to a questionable news source
estimates.value_raw: Table 4, Gab column: Posts containing a URL 3,778; Matched 0.47; Questionable 0.38; Reliable 0.62

estimates.definition: The post's external link points to a news outlet that MBFC classifies as Questionable or as Conspiracy-Pseudoscience; the authors' binary label groups both as 'Questionable'.
estimates.misinfo_def: "by questionable information source we mean a news outlet systematically showing one or more of the following characteristics: extreme bias, consistent promotion of propaganda/conspiracies, poor or no sourcing to credible information, information not supported by evidence or unverifiable, a complete lack of transparency and/or fake news."

estimates.ground_truth_detail: Media Bias/Fact Check (MBFC), an independent fact-checking organisation, classifies news outlets by Factual/Sourcing into Conspiracy-Pseudoscience, Pro-Science or Questionable; the authors collapsed Questionable + Conspiracy-Pseudoscience into 'Questionable' and everything else into 'Reliable'. Of the 2,637 MBFC outlets retrieved, 800 were Questionable and 1,837 Reliable. The authors explicitly flag 'the limits of an approach that is based on labelling news outlets rather than single articles'. No reliability statistics.
estimates.moderator_quote: We consider all the posts in our dataset that contain at least one URL linking to a website outside the related social media platfrom (e.g., tweets pointing outside Twitter). We separate URLs in two main categories obtained using the classification provided by MediaBias/FactCheck (MBFC).
estimates.notes: The denominator is the MATCHED subset only (47% on Gab), not all URL-posts: unmatched domains, including links to other social platforms, are excluded, which inflates the questionable share relative to all shared links. The matched count is derived (0.47 x 3,778) and is therefore approximate; the extracted VALUE (0.38) is verbatim from Table 4. Gab is coded platform_norm = other (not in the controlled list); the paper describes it as a Twitter-like, lightly moderated platform with a far-right user base. source_quote is the whole of Table 4 as one contiguous span (the table is the only place the value appears); this row reads the Gab column.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The regression coefficients rho (Table 7) are RATIOS of questionable to reliable volumes, not shares of a whole: posts Gab 0.695, Reddit 0.047, YouTube 0.073, Twitter 0.110; reactions Gab 2.721. Converting them into shares would require a complement/sum I constructed, which R8 forbids, and they duplicate the Table 4 information. (2) The amplification factors (Table 2: E_U/E_R = alpha, Gab 3.9, Reddit 0.55, Twitter 0.97, YouTube 0.35, with E_U/E_R values 5.6/1.4, 22.7/40.1, 15.1/15.6, 1.4x10^4/3.9x10^4) are mean engagement per post, not prevalence shares; no Instagram values are given. (3) R0 estimates (Table 1) are diffusion parameters, not prevalence. (4) 'Matched' fractions (0.47, 0.55, 0.035, 0.09, 0.27) measure matching ability against the MBFC list, not misinformation. (5) Table 5 gives the fraction of URLs pointing to other social platforms, again not a misinformation share. (6) No exposure, reach, recall or concentration measure is reported: the paper measures posting volumes and engagement, not who saw what. (7) The construct call is the main judgement here: the denominator is user posts carrying an external link, i.e. shared links, so SHARING/content_share follows the rule that '% of shared links unreliable' is SHARING. A CONTENT reading (a share of the items that exist in a keyword corpus) is defensible; if an adjudicator prefers it, the same five values and denominators apply with denom_scope still topical.

rob.design: Observational cross-platform content analysis. Keyword-driven collection from Google Trends COVID-19 queries (coronavirus, pandemic, coronaoutbreak, china, wuhan, nCoV, IamNotAVirus, coronavirus_update, coronavirus_transmission, coronavirusnews, coronavirusoutbreak) across five platforms, 1 January - 14 February 2020 (Twitter 27 January - 14 February because of API limits): 1,342,103 posts, 7,465,721 comments, 3,734,815 users (Table 3). Collection methods differ by platform and are non-probability: Reddit via the Pushshift.io archive; Gab via keyword-derived hashtags selected manually; YouTube via the Data API plus algorithmic related-video crawling; Twitter via the 1% stream plus rate-limited search; Instagram manually compiled with no API. Misinformation identified at the SOURCE level: posts with an external URL matched against Media Bias/Fact Check (2,637 outlets: 800 Questionable, 1,837 Reliable), with Questionable + Conspiracy-Pseudoscience collapsed into one label. Matching rates are low to moderate (0.035-0.55), so each platform's share rests on a matched subset of unknown representativeness. No inter-rater reliability or validation of the MBFC labels is reported, and the authors themselves flag outlet-level labelling as a limitation.
rob.item6_quote: Thus, by questionable information source we mean a news outlet systematically showing one or more of the following characteristics: extreme bias, consistent promotion of propaganda/conspiracies, poor or no sourcing to credible information, information not supported by evidence or unverifiable, a complete lack of transparency and/or fake news. By reliable information sources we mean news outlets that do not show any of the aforementioned characteristics.
rob.item10_quote: We consider all the posts in our dataset that contain at least one URL linking to a website outside the related social media platfrom (e.g., tweets pointing outside Twitter). ... Considering all the 2637 news outlets that we retrieve from the list provided by MBFC we end up with 800 outlets classified as Questionable 1837 outlets classified as Reliable. Using such a classification we quantify our overall ability to match and label domains of posts containing URLs, as reported in Table 4.
